idea.title: Shyp: tap an app, a courier picks up, packs and ships

source.text: Shyp: tap an app and a courier picks up, packs and ships any item for $5 plus postage, launch country US. Score it as of 2014-03-01: use only evidence published on or before that date (set verdict.as_of). Founder: a seed-funded startup. Just go: do not ask questions. Use the slug shyp.

idea.problem: Shipping an item means finding a box, packing it, printing a label and queuing at a post office or carrier store.
idea.customer: San Francisco smartphone owners (25-34 professionals) and small online sellers shipping a few parcels a month
idea.solution: iPhone app: a courier picks up any item at your door, Shyp packs it and ships it with the best carrier rate.
claims: a courier picks up, packs and ships any item for $5 plus postage
assumptions: Launch city is San Francisco, where the private beta runs
Average postage about USD 12 per shipment
Couriers are per-pickup contractors, as reported in 2013

confidence.note: Unit costs are estimates: no pre-2014 source for SF courier wages, packing costs or Shyp order density

gross_margin.note: Est. -$3.4/order: $6.32 revenue vs ~$9.70 courier, packing and card cost; costs_eat_margin hit (R5 <=2)

ltv_cac.note: Negative contribution per order makes LTV negative against an est. $30 CAC

pricing_power.note: Free USPS pickup anchors pickup at $0; Shyp itself waives the $5 fee for 2+ items

build_effort.note: App plus courier ops plus packing hub; private beta already running with ~10 couriers

skills_match.note: Seed-funded team already operating a beta in SF; ops scaling skill unproven

capital_needed.note: $2.1M seed covers a one-city launch; multi-city ops need far more

time_to_mvp.note: Paid private beta live in SF by 2013-09

sales_cycle.note: Consumer impulse purchase: tap, pickup, pay the same day

channel_readiness.note: SF tech press and investor audience; iPhone loyal-user cost $1.33-1.90 in 2013

search_demand.note: USPS ships ~3.7B parcels a year (est.); no app keyword data found

trend.note: USPS package volume +6% FY2013; US e-commerce +16.9% in 2013

willingness_to_pay.note: Pickup is free from USPS; no evidence of a paid waitlist or price rises

free_alternatives.note: USPS free pickup and boxes cover part of the job; the user still packs and prints

competitor_density.note: No direct pickup-pack-ship rival found; Postmates and TaskRabbit are adjacent

differentiation.note: Packing plus pickup bundle is specific, but Postmates has ~900 SF couriers to copy it

legal_regulatory.note: Per-pickup contractors in CA amid driver class actions; packer owns hazmat screening

platform_dependency.note: Relies on carrier rates and terms (UPS +4.9% in 2014); no Apple cut on services

market_risk.note: Shipping is a durable need; on-demand errands like Exec stalled outside SF

skills.note: Seed-funded founding team; no prior logistics track record found

assets.note: Investor network (Homebrew, Tim Ferriss) gives press and reach

interest.note: Founder motivation not documented in sources

sam.reasoning: SF ~840k residents x 56% smartphone = 470k x 1 parcel/month x $5 fee x 12 = $28M fee revenue

som.reasoning: 4.7k-14k early users (1-3% of SF smartphone adults) x 1 order/month x $5 x 12 = $0.3-0.84M, midpoint ~$0.5M

competitor_price_range.value: USD 0 (USPS pickup) to 10 (TaskRabbit Deliver Now flat)

variable_cost_per_unit.reasoning: courier batched mid $4.9 + packing mid ~$4 + card fee $0.79 = $9.70, minus $1.32 postage spread kept (11% Commercial Base x $12) = $8.38 net

gross_margin_pct.reasoning: ($5 fee - $8.38 net variable cost) / $5 = -68%; contribution -$3.38 per order

expected_lifetime.reasoning: Localytics 2013: 34% of users open an app 11+ times, 22% once; assume ~6 paid shipments per retained customer per year

cac.reasoning: Fiksu cost per loyal iPhone user $1.33-1.90 (2013) x ~15-20 to reach a paying, repeat customer = $20-38, midpoint ~$30

ltv_cac.reasoning: LTV -$20 / CAC $30 = -0.68: every customer loses money until route density lowers courier cost

payback_months.reasoning: Monthly gross profit per customer is negative (-$3.38 x 0.5 orders/month), so CAC is never paid back

fixed_costs_month.reasoning: $2.1M seed / ~21 months runway = ~$100k/month (team, SF packing hub, insurance)

break_even_customers_per_month.reasoning: Only if contribution reaches +$2/order via density and pricing: $100k fixed / $2 = 50,000 orders/month

verdict.launch_reason: Shyp's private beta runs in San Francisco, with dense demand and its investor network.
verdict.cheapest_test: Run 7 days of batched 1-hour pickup windows at a per-item fee on 200 beta orders and measure contribution per order and pickups per courier-hour.
kill_criteria: Fewer than 3 pickups per courier-hour by day 7 -> stop expansion and rework routing
Contribution per order below USD 0 after 200 orders -> do not raise more for consumer on-demand
Under 20% of first-time users order again within 30 days -> stop paid acquisition

rescue.change: Sell to SF eBay/Etsy sellers and small shops with scheduled daily pickups instead of on-demand consumers
rescue.why: Fixes costs_eat_margin and ltv_cac: dense, recurring routes lift contribution and repeat rate
rescue.requires: B2B sales motion and seller-community partnerships

rescue.change: Charge per item (drop the 2+ item waiver), add a packing fee and batch pickups into 1-hour windows
rescue.why: Fixes gross_margin: est. contribution moves from -$3.4 to about +$1 per order
rescue.requires: Routing logic and a price test on beta users

rescue.change: Hire couriers as part-time W-2 employees from launch
rescue.why: Fixes legal_platform_risk: removes CA misclassification exposure before scale
rescue.requires: Payroll, workers' comp and higher density to absorb cost

type_checks.note: No pre-2014 App Store keyword popularity data found for shipping apps; first users come from press and word of mouth
Apple's in-app purchase cut applied to digital goods, not physical services; Shyp charges cards directly (no dated pre-2014 guideline copy found)

narrative.answer: **PIVOT** at 59. Demand and timing are real (parcels +6%, e-commerce +16.9%), but at $5 with packing included and the fee waived for 2+ items, each order **loses money** until route density arrives, and courier classification is a California legal risk.
tldr: Demand is real and rising: USPS parcels **+6%** in FY2013, US e-commerce **+16.9%** in 2013.
Unit economics are **negative** at launch: est. -$3.4 per order before route density.
No direct rival, but free USPS pickup sets the anchor at **$0** and Postmates could copy the bundle.

key_findings.title: Each order loses money at launch
key_findings.detail: Est. **$6.32** revenue per order vs ~$9.70 courier, packing and card cost; the fee is waived for 2+ items (estimate).

key_findings.title: Free USPS pickup anchors the price
key_findings.detail: USPS picks up **free** for Click-N-Ship labels and mails free boxes; Shyp's real premium is packing and no printer.

key_findings.title: Courier classification is a live risk
key_findings.detail: Shyp pays contracted couriers per pickup while a delivery driver class (~**3,700** drivers) was certified in 2013.

narrative.recommendation: Keep the beta, but do not scale consumer on-demand yet: charge per item, batch pickups into 1-hour windows and test a scheduled-pickup offer for SF online sellers for 7 days.
narrative.steelman: Parcel volume and e-commerce are growing fast, no one bundles pickup with packing, and a well-funded team can win on density: at **3+ pickups per courier-hour** the economics turn positive. The evidence supports demand, but density at Shyp is unproven.

premortem.cause: Courier and packing cost per order stays above the $5 fee, so burn grows with every order.
premortem.early_signal: Fewer than 2 pickups per courier-hour in the first 30 days

premortem.cause: A misclassification claim forces couriers onto payroll, raising cost per pickup by 20-30%.
premortem.early_signal: Courier pay complaints or turnover above 30% a month

premortem.cause: Consumers ship a few times a year, so CAC is never recovered.
premortem.early_signal: Under 20% of first-time users order again within 30 days

why_now.note: Smartphone ownership crossed half of US adults and on-demand delivery is drawing venture money, so the window is open.

changes.what: 56% of US adults own a smartphone, 81% of ages 25-34.
USPS package volume grew 6% while letter mail fell.
Postmates raised a $16M Series B for on-demand delivery.
Shyp raised $250k on AngelList in 53 minutes under new general solicitation rules.

free_alternative.evidence: USPS offers free pickup for Click-N-Ship labels and free Priority boxes (2013-12), but the user still packs and prints: partial, not whole job.

strong_competitor.evidence: Searched on-demand pickup, pack and ship in the US before 2014-03: 0 direct rivals; Postmates, TaskRabbit, Zipments, eBay pilots are adjacent.

graveyard.evidence: Kozmo.com closed 9 markets in 2001-04; Exec shut its errands service in 2013-09, losing money and unable to scale beyond SF.

no_distribution.evidence: Channel exists: SF tech press, investor audiences and iPhone installs at $1.33-1.90 per loyal user (Fiksu, 2013).

costs_eat_margin.evidence: Est. $6.32 revenue per order ($5 fee + 11% Commercial Base spread on $12 postage) vs ~$9.70 courier, packing and card cost (estimate).

weak_demand.evidence: USPS package volume +6% in FY2013 and US e-commerce +16.9% in 2013: rising.

legal_platform_risk.evidence: Per-pickup contracted couriers in CA while a nationwide class of ~3,700 delivery drivers was certified (2013-06); packer bears hazmat screening.

saturated_wave.evidence: Searched TechCrunch and Product Hunt for 2013-03 to 2014-02: no near-identical consumer pickup-and-ship launches found.

test_plan.step: Switch beta pricing to $5 per item plus a $2 packing fee; announce 1-hour pickup windows
test_plan.verify: At least 50 beta users see the new price

test_plan.step: Batch pickups by neighborhood and log courier time per order
Offer scheduled daily pickups to 30 SF eBay/Etsy sellers
Compute contribution per order over 200 orders
